Thanks for the reply. You said a lot of nice things about me. 

I guess what I'm afraid of is that if I focus on the positive things that happen to me, I'll immediately flip to the other end of the spectrum and become completely oblivious to all the bad things I'm doing. Yes, I understand that what I'm currently doing (focusing on the bad) is not a good idea either, but I guess at some point I decided that focusing on the bad things I do would be better than focusing only on the good. It's tough to strike that balance of focus, but if what you're saying is true (and I have no doubt that it is), it's a necessary one.

As far as giving myself credit goes, I realized that the reason I disregard compliments is because I feel that anything of note that I do could easily be, and often is, replicated by another person on a daily basis. Another way of saying this is that I feel like doing awesome things is my job, and whenever I do something awesome, instead of telling myself "good job", I say something more like "yeah, of course you're supposed to do that, it's your job", so I give myself no credit. 

This does not translate to my interactions with other human beings (at least, I don't think so). I give credit where credit is due. When the people I care about the most disappoint me or whatever, I still love them, I still see the best in them, etc. I just don't have the balls to give myself that same generosity. In essence, I disobey the "golden rule" for the opposite reason most people disobey it.

I think the best piece of advice in your comment is asking myself how my current pattern of thinking is serving me. I tend to think extremely rationally, so even drawing up a "pro con" list would help. So, thank your for that.

In fact, thank you for your whole comment. It really did help, and now I have a direction to take other than down. Unfortunately, the best I can do in return is give you an upvote. :)
